LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 8.1.1ATTENTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 8.1: Listening and Speaking 8.1.1Attentive Listening

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Listening and Speaking 8.1.1Attentive Listening. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How should we respond to instructions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify nouns in singular and plural forms from a song for information
2. respond to verbal instructions for information

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Listening and Speaking 8.1.1Attentive Listening helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Work with peers to list cultural foods on charts,
2. Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner contributes to group decision making when working with peers to collect varied songs on the theme from the community.
3. Digital Literacy: This is promoted as the learner interacts with digital content when listening to recordings about various cultural foods. Values:
4. Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits a self-driven attitude when organising the songs collected in the class portfolio.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
